title: Redispatch prefetch POC weekly review

transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-10-14
Start Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood SE), Samir (NoviQ Eng Mgr), Lena (NoviQ ML Eng), Jordan (NoviQ SRE), Ava (NoviQ Product)

Auto-summary (auto): Weekly POC check-in; discussed decreasing KV miss tail by redispatching low confidence prefixes to cheaper hosted variant, tuning eviction window, and improved metric instrumentation. Agreed on heatmap and on-prem benchmark.

00:00 Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone thanks for joining — I think we've got most folks, quick roll call?
00:05 Samir (NoviQ): yeah Samir here, Lena, Jordan and Ava are on as well, hi Maya.
00:08 Maya: sweet. Quick agenda — hit rates review, redispatch idea, eviction tuning, instrumentation gaps, next steps — any additions?
00:15 Samir: no, good. we really want to see where the misses are concentrated, last week the hit rate exploded low in evenings so curious.
00:20 Ethan (Redwood): cool, I'll start with the numbers we pulled. note — these are from the staging agent hooked to the KV cache; we saw an overall KV hit-rate of 67% last 48 hours, but the prefix-level distribution is heavy tailed.
00:30 Ethan: (screen share ref) so here's the key-frequency histogram, the top 10% of prefixes account for ~72% of hits, the rest are very sparse — that's consistent with conversational apps where many one-off user ids or long prompts appear.
00:45 Lena (NoviQ): yeah that matches our telemetry — chat threads with long system prompts are killing the reuse.
00:48 Priya (Redwood): one quick callout — the extractor we used for prefixing likely over-trims occasionally, so some keys that *could* match are slightly different; I'll put the extractor config we used into the doc link in the notes.
01:05 Samir: okay, low-hitrate prefixes — what's the proposed redispatch behavior? you mentioned fallback to hosted smaller model?
01:12 Ethan: right. idea is: if a prefix's moving-window hit probability drops below X (we prototyped X=12%), we can redispatch that request to either a higher cache-sensitivity route (more aggressive prefetch) or to a hosted smaller-quantized model to keep latency lower and cost predictable — basically graceful degradation.
01:30 Jordan (NoviQ): are we talking about runtime redispatch (in the edge router), or a pre-batch decision? concern is double-cost if we prefetch and then re-run.
01:40 Ethan: good point. our plan is router-level quick decision: consult a small in-memory table of recent prefix hit rates (very lightweight) — if below threshold, route to fallback lane; no double-execution. only when attempt to rehydrate cache do we pay that cost.
01:58 Ava (NoviQ): can we see an example flow? like user sends long chat, prefix misses, what happens and what UX impact?
02:05 Priya: sure, example A: user prompt arrives, KV consult returns miss, router checks prefix-table — sees low score — routes to hosted small model variant with shorter context window. response returns faster and cheaper but with slightly lower quality. fallback to full model only if user triggers explicit long-form generation.
02:25 Lena: hmm that might be acceptable for discovery flows; for core tasks we need to ensure quality. can we do canary percent?
02:30 Maya: yeah we have rollout controls — canary and percent-based routing, also automatic fallback if quality is flagged.
02:36 Samir: what's the metric for 'quality flagged'? we don't have ground truth during live traffic.
02:40 Ethan: we've got a lightweight heuristic: token-level perplexity delta and repetition signals, plus a small sampled eval set that we keep for this pilot. if the smaller model deviates a lot we trigger steer-back to primary. it's noisy but workable for pilot.
03:00 Jordan: instrumenting that requires more metrics on the NoviQ side — we need exposure to token-level latencies and model-side logs, is that doable?
03:10 Samir: yes we can add a sidecar logging endpoint. Jordan will confirm any production constraints.
03:15 Jordan: noted. I'll check redis timeouts and whether our ingress will drop long requests — especially since some prefetch attempts are synchronous.
03:25 Ethan: also we noticed a cluster of misses around certain system prompt templates — likely due to slight whitespace or metadata differences. Priya's extractor note aims to normalize that.
03:38 Priya: leaning into more aggressive canonicalization of system prefixes increased hit-rate by ~4 points in early tests but also increases false positives — tradeoff.
03:48 Lena: we worry about false positives causing stale context reuse — that would be bad for correctness.
03:52 Priya: totally — we should set a conservative canonicalization strategy and validate on a offline dataset first.
04:05 Maya: eviction policy — current default evicts LRU at 24 hours, but we saw some useful prefixes live across days. Thoughts?
04:12 Ethan: suggested adaptive TTL keyed by last-access frequency: hot prefixes get longer TTL, sparse ones shorter. in our sim it moved effective hit-rate from 67 to 71%.
04:28 Samir: does that make memory balloons? we have quotas.
04:31 Ethan: we'll propose a capped tier system — e.g., dedicated hotset memory and separate cold ring; you can limit hotset size.
04:40 Jordan: need to understand memory vs cost. can we simulate at your end and send memory curves?
04:44 Ethan: yes we'll push a memory-usage curve per TTL policy into the doc.
04:50 Maya: instrumentation gaps — what metrics are missing from NoviQ?
04:54 Jordan: token-level latencies, redis miss reasons (timeout vs not-found), and per-prefix hit counters are the big ones. also need trace IDs correlated to model runs.
05:05 Maya: action — Jordan to expose two endpoints and we will consume; Ethan to update instrumentation plan.
05:12 Samir: about eviction and prefetch — is prefetch synchronous or background?
05:16 Priya: prefetch can be background (async) when we predict near-future hits, but we also do synchronous prefetch for very high-confidence prefixes to avoid tail latency.
05:28 Lena: what's our confidence threshold?
05:30 Ethan: for async prefetch we used 45% predicted hit in next-minute; for sync prefetch 85%+. those numbers are tunable.
05:40 Samir: curious about the evening drop — is it traffic pattern or misclassification?
05:44 Ethan: preliminary look: evenings have more short exploratory queries leading to cold-start prefixes; also our prefix extractor is more likely to include user-specific tokens in those cases.
05:58 Priya: if you can share a couple of log samples (scrubbed) we can refine extractor rules.
06:05 Samir: yes, we can do that. We'll sanitize PII.
06:10 Ava: small ask — can we get price implications per million requests if we enable redispatch to hosted small variant?
06:15 Maya: yes we'll include a price delta in the pricing doc; early estimate is +0.6 cents per 1k requests in worst case but depends on how much is routed to fallback.
06:28 Lena: ok. Jordan — any infra blockers for pilot scale?
06:32 Jordan: redis is fine but need to tune maxclients; also we need to ensure KMS calls for on-prem don't add too much latency when decrypting embeddings.
06:40 Ethan: noted. For on-prem benchmark we need a small window to run an end-to-end experiment — can we commit to week of 2026-10-25?
06:46 Samir: yes that works tentatively.
06:50 Maya: cool. any security/compliance questions?
06:52 Ava: we need to see a SOC2 summary and encryption at rest details for hosted fallback lane.
06:58 Maya: I'll attach the security pack in follow-up.
07:05 Priya: quick note on prefix coalescing — we tried a heuristic where semantically-similar templates map to the same canonical prefix; that gave a smaller bump but required more offline vetting.
07:20 Lena: we should test that in a shadow run not live.
07:24 Ethan: agreed. we'll run shadow traffic split for 48 hours on the sim cluster.
07:30 Samir: what's the success criteria for the pilot end? do we aim for X% hit-rate uplift or cost per request target?
07:36 Maya: proposed success: increase effective KV hit-rate by at least 6 points and reduce 95th tail latency by 20% or keep cost increase under 10% — flexible, open to negotiation.
07:50 Samir: sounds reasonable. can you put that in the doc so our PM approves?
07:54 Maya: will do.
08:00 Jordan: quick technical question — if we do redispatch to smaller model, how do you handle KV reuse across models? is KV format compatible?
08:08 Ethan: KV is model-agnostic for prefix strings; the cached token embeddings are versioned — we maintain serializer versions and a compatibility shim. small caveat on quantized kernels but we've handled that in previous pilots.
08:24 Lena: ok good.
08:30 Priya: I'll add a note about serializer compat in the repo. link in follow-up.
08:36 Maya: last bit — next steps recap. Ethan to produce heatmap and memory curves by Fri (2026-10-16). Jordan to confirm redis/timeouts and surface rate limiters by 2026-10-17. Maya to send pricing and security pack by 2026-10-18. Schedule on-prem benchmark for week of 2026-10-25.
08:58 Samir: good. And please mark items in the pilot doc so our procurement sees the SLO options.
09:05 Maya: will do. thanks everyone.
09:10 Meeting end.
